units: <cite ref="Menachot 68b:24">Men. 68ᵇ</cite> <he>מהנך דאַשְׁרוּשׁ וכ׳</he> of that barley that has taken root before the ʿOmer time.
<cite ref="Gittin 22a:6">Gitt. 22ᵃ</cite> <he>בדאשרוש כולי וכ׳</he> when the planted trees have taken root, all agree (that they are subject to tithes); a. e.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 80:10">Targ. Ps. LXXX, 10</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Ecclesiastes 3:2">Targ. Koh. III, 2</cite>.

senses.gloss: (v. P. Sm. 4340) [to expand,] to bring profit, benefit.
units: <cite ref="Moed Katan 12a:6">M. Kat. 12ᵃ</cite> <he>כיון … שָׁרָשׁוּיְי … מְשָׁרְשׁוּ ליה וכ׳</he> since they receive no wages, they (by working for him during the festive week) only intend to benefit him.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 82a:7">B. Bath. 82ᵃ</cite> <he>למחפר ולמִשְּׁרַשׁ קיימי</he> ed. (Ms. M. <he>לחפור ולשרש</he> Hebr.) they are liable to be dug for and taken out (when they cease to bear fruit).
<cite ref="Bava Batra 82a:6">Ib.</cite> <he>למיחפר ולשרש</he> (corr. acc., or <he>לחפור ולשרש</he>).

<cite ref="Gittin 35a:4">Gitt. 35ᵃ</cite> <he>א׳ לה מקום דינר</he> (Rashi <he>אשתרש</he>) she saved as much dough (in the bread which she gave away) as would have been in the space which was occupied by the Denar (that came into it).
<cite ref="Gittin 44a">Ib. 44ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Chullin 131a:3">Ḥull. 131ᵃ</cite> <he>קא מִשְׁתָּרְשֵׁי ליה</he> he is benefited (by being released from a debt).

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 42b:14">B. Mets. 42ᵇ</cite> <he>והא קא משתרשי ליה</he> but did he not have the benefit (of using his neighbor’s cuscuta for brewing and saving his own? why, then, should he not indemnify his neighbor?).

<cite ref="Ketubot 108a:3">Keth. 108ᵃ</cite> <he>הא קא משתרשי ליה</he> is he (for whom the debt was paid) not benefited? (better <he>הא קא מְשָׁרְשֵׁי ליה</he> does he who pays the debt for him not benefit him?, v. supra).
